sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Checks for the summary converter
sections.what: Three checks: build identifiers and timing numbers stay out of the findings, real domain values like planned months and zero counts stay in, and excluded names also apply to nested fields without changing the original summary.
sections.why: The test names state the reason: the owner should see results, not technical record data.
sections.watch_out: A change to the hidden-name rules can break these checks, which is their purpose, but a new hidden name needs a new check.

summary: Automated checks that the stage summary converter hides build ids and timing numbers, keeps real domain values such as months and counts, and never changes the saved summary.
purpose: Protects the rule that the owner sees real results, not build details.
why: The test names state the rules being protected. Reason for the specific cases is inferred from those names.
how: 1. Runs three checks with the built-in Node test runner. 2. Each check builds a sample summary and calls the converter. 3. Compares the labels and values with the expected ones, or checks the original data is unchanged.
inputs: Sample summary objects written inside the test.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each check.
risks: The checks only cover the sample cases. Other rules, such as tone and time formatting, are not tested here.
debug: Run the test file with Node's test runner. A failing check prints the expected and actual values, so compare them against the rules in the converter.
